Implements [spec 0008](../specs/features/001-mvp/specs/0008-web-admin.md).
Source and executable tests are canonical after implementation.

## Reconnaissance

`apps/web/src/main.tsx` is a bootstrap placeholder, with no existing browser
forms, request helpers, window state, or test doubles. Server routes already
cover roots/scans, catalog, collections/membership, channel lifecycle,
programming blocks, schedule and current state. Reuse those routes and
`startTestServer`, catalog fixtures, and existing scheduling eligibility policy.
The requested desktop supersedes section navigation and the spec's design-system
non-goal. Accepted ADRs require no change. Read-only setup and collection-status
projections supply missing MVP facts; no new domain policy belongs in the web.

### WEB-001: Desktop shell and window transitions

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-05. Delivered original vector branding and wallpaper,
XP chrome, boot, shortcuts, Start, taskbar/tray and accessible singleton window
transitions. Persistent layouts, snap and authentication remain deferred.

**Goal**: Boot into an original XP desktop with usable singleton programs.

**Scope**: Tokens, vector branding/icons/wallpaper, boot, shortcuts, Start,
taskbar/tray, window reducer, drag, keyboard movement, minimize/maximize/restore,
focus and close, viewport recovery, reduced motion.

**Out of scope**: Authentication, persistent layouts, snap, OS applets.

**Blocking dependencies**: Bootstrap spec 0001.

**Implementation notes**: Keep generic window state separate from program
contents; preserve mounted minimized forms and suspend their polling.

**Verification**: Deterministic reducer and rendered interaction tests; browser
checks at wide and narrow sizes.

**Docs impact**: Reconcile spec 0008; record original artwork/reference provenance.

### WEB-002: Catalog and collections programs

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-05. Delivered root configuration/scans/catalog and collection
creation, renaming and membership editing, with backend eligibility status.
Minimized collection drafts survive refreshed reads on restore.

**Goal**: Add/scan media roots and build explicitly ordered collections.

**Scope**: API client/request states, roots/scan/catalog, collection create,
rename, membership add/remove/reorder, backend schedulability projection.

**Out of scope**: Background scan jobs, browser eligibility policy.

**Blocking dependencies**: WEB-001 and existing catalog/collection routes.

**Implementation notes**: Reuse backend `isSchedulableMedia`, and testing
fixtures. Guard stale reads and cancel requests when their owner closes.

**Verification**: API contract tests, rendered form/scan/order tests.

**Docs impact**: Document additive status endpoint in spec 0008.

### WEB-003: Channels, programming and observations

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-05. Delivered channel identity/lifecycle, programming sources,
guide/current-state observations and visible-only polling. Cleanup retries survive
program close and committed changes remain visible even if follow-up reads fail.

**Goal**: Configure channel programming and inspect backend-derived broadcasts.

**Scope**: Channel CRUD/enable/disable, saved-change cleanup retry, programming
source/mode, schedule, current/next program and offset, visible-only 10s refresh.

**Out of scope**: Scheduling algorithms, telemetry or FFmpeg changes.

**Blocking dependencies**: WEB-002 and implemented channel/schedule/state routes.

**Implementation notes**: Keep failed-cleanup records independent of deleted
channel rows; honor `persistenceCommitted: false` on a rejected re-enable.

**Verification**: Rendered cleanup retry, source payload, stale channel read and
poll visibility tests; existing server contracts remain passing.

**Docs impact**: Preserve backend authority and cleanup semantics in spec.

### WEB-004: Plex setup and acceptance verification

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-05. Delivered configured setup URLs, copy feedback and
instructions, with Chromium setup-flow coverage at desktop and narrow sizes.
Real Plex tuning, spike retirement and production hosting remain separate work.

**Goal**: Finish the daily administration loop with actual configured URLs.

**Scope**: Backend `/plex/setup` projection, copy feedback, concise instructions,
accessibility, wide/narrow browser verification and judgment review.

**Out of scope**: Plex authentication, spike retirement, production hosting.

**Blocking dependencies**: WEB-003; accepted adapter contract in spec 0007.

**Implementation notes**: Reuse server Plex settings; never infer public URLs
from browser location. Do not change PLX-005 status or retire the spike here.

**Verification**: Host-spoofing setup contract test; normal exit checks plus
build and browser checks. Record any unavailable verification explicitly.

**Docs impact**: User README usage and completed ticket Status blocks.

## Judgment Review Evidence

- Reuse searches covered fetch/cancellation, form text, window transitions,
  collection ordering, `src/testing/` and integration suites. The web bootstrap
  had no usable browser helpers. Server `sendApiError` is a Fastify reply writer,
  not a browser error reader; process/runtime doubles are not fetch transports.
  Browser callers share `formText`, `resourcePath`, request hooks and
  `scheduleWindowPath` rather than copying these behaviors between programs.
- The added kraziBrain export `isSchedulableMedia` has one production package
  consumer: the collection-status route. It reuses the existing integer-duration
  policy; the browser only renders its projection. `/plex/setup` reads the same
  parsed settings as tuner routes, proven with a spoofed Host contract test.
- Resource publication checks caller cancellation after JSON parsing; writes
  check owner lifetime after await. `use-resource.test.ts` deliberately resolves
  held responses after selection replacement and close, and tests visible-only
  polling plus slow reads. Clipboard feedback also checks component lifetime.
  Collection and programming tests distinguish saved state from preserved drafts.
- `BrowserApi` returns HTTP responses and nested server error envelopes, including
  204 deletes and both values of `persistenceCommitted`. It deliberately ignores
  abort for race tests. Chromium tests additionally consume actual Fastify routes
  and SQLite, reusing `startTestServer`, `ControlledProber`, `PROBE_RESULT` and
  temporary-directory cleanup rather than duplicating backend doubles.
- No new stateful production class, persistent domain model, scheduling policy,
  FFmpeg ownership or subscriber cancellation is introduced; those review
  categories do not apply. Shell transitions remain a small presentation reducer.
  The strict audit has no errors or review items in touched files.

## Verification Boundaries

Chromium screenshots are inspected at 1280×800 and 390×844. Browser coverage
uses controlled probing and does not claim real ffprobe, FFmpeg or Plex tuning.
Those opt-in binary suites are not required because packaging/probing/runtime
code is unchanged. The standard media suite may skip its existing symlink case
on Windows when this user cannot create file symlinks.
